gloss: royal fern; fiddlehead of the royal fern (edible wild plant)

definitions.gloss: royal fern; its coiled young shoots eaten as a wild vegetable
definitions.explanation: A fern whose tightly curled spring shoots are gathered as {山菜|さんさい} (wild mountain vegetables). The shoots must be boiled and soaked before eating, and are often sold dried.

examples.japanese: ぜんまいの{煮物|にもの}が{好|す}きだ。
{春|はる}になると{山|やま}でぜんまいを{採|と}る。
examples.english: When spring comes, we gather royal fern in the mountains.

examples.japanese: {干|ほ}したぜんまいは{水|みず}で{戻|もど}してから{油|あぶら}で{炒|いた}めると{美味|おい}しい。
examples.english: Dried royal fern is delicious if you rehydrate it in water and then stir-fry it in oil.

notes:
Usually written in kana; the kanji {薇|ぜんまい} is rare. One of the classic {山菜|さんさい} of early spring, along with {蕨|わらび} and ふきのとう.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ぜんまいの{煮物|にもの}: simmered royal fern
- ぜんまいを{採|と}る: to gather royal fern
- {干|ほ}しぜんまい: dried royal fern
- ぜんまいのナムル: royal fern namul (a common Korean-style side dish)

HOMONYM:
The same-sounding ぜんまい also means a coiled spring or clockwork mechanism (ぜんまいを{巻|ま}く, to wind up a spring) — the plant's tight spiral is the source of that sense.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {蕨|わらび}: bracken — another spring fern shoot, thinner and used for {蕨餅|わらびもち} starch
- ふきのとう: butterbur bud — bitter, and eaten as tempura or miso rather than simmered
